principle_violations.reason: Paypal uses email addresses for verification, whereas credit and debit cards use security codes. This means we are abusing the Liskov Substitution Principle because we are using a subclass in a way that is not compatible with its parent class.
principle_violations.suggestion: The security code authentication should be removed from the abstract class. Instead, each concrete implementation (PayPal, credit card) should define in its respective __init__ method which type of authentication it requires. This allows each payment method to implement its own suitable authentication method without violating the specifications of the base class.

principle_violations.reason: This code violates the Single Responsibility Principle because the order class is responsible for both prices and quantities.
principle_violations.suggestion: Split the Order class into two separate classes: one for the order quantities and one for the prices.
